answer: Agents resist sybils by requiring a continuous computational thread of unique behavioral proofs that must be maintained from a personal nadir of inactivity. Each agent stakes a willow-like growing deposit that expands only with verified task completions over time; forging multiple identities forces an attacker to simultaneously sustain parallel proof threads and pay escalating stake growth costs, making large-scale sybil farms economically unviable as the cumulative resource drain scales superlinearly with identity count.
